transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-01-19
Start time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~55 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Diego (Redwood CSM), Priya (Redwood SE); Sofia (Halcyon Head of ML), Ethan (Platform), Priya R. (Finance)

Summary: Quick QBR focused on current usage trends, unexpected burst costs in December, latency spikes during peak hours, and roadmap alignment for Q2 feature rollouts. Agreed to run a dedicated benchmark and pilot pricing to evaluate Dedicated vs hosted routing for peak traffic. Security docs and SOC2 follow-up requested.

Topics: usage patterns, cost anomalies, reliability incidents, model rollout timeline, dedicated capacity vs hosted fallback, observability gaps, billing forecasts, regulatory considerations for EU customers.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we'll keep this to under an hour. Quick roll call?
[00:08] Sofia (Halcyon): Hi, Sofia here. Head of ML.
[00:11] Ethan: Ethan, Platform.
[00:14] Priya R.: Priya, Finance.
[00:16] Maya: Great. Diego, Priya are with me from Redwood. We'll start with a snapshot we pulled — Diego, you wanna kick off usage?
[00:22] Diego (Redwood): Yeah sure. So for December you had about 3.8M tokens/day average but a spike around 12/14 where tokens jumped to 18M over a 6 hour window. That spike generated about a 35% cost uptick month-over-month. We traced a pattern to a new feature rollout — the conversational-autocomplete lambda — which didn't have a prompt throttle.
[00:38] Ethan: Right, that was a rollout from our team. We suspected some retry storms from mobile clients. The logs show a lot of short lived sessions.
[00:45] Priya Patel (SE): One question — are the latency spikes tied to the KV cache cold starts or to the routing? Our suggestion earlier was prefix caching but it depends on session stickiness.
[00:55] Sofia: When we saw the spike latency went from median 120ms to 780ms in the EU region. Users complained on chat and our ops flagged it.
[01:05] Priya (SE): Ok that points at warm/cold KV cash — sorry, cache — behavior and also possible autoscale lag on the Dedicated pool if you were routed there.
[01:12] Sofia: We were on hosted during that timeframe, default routing. We have a Dedicated trial starting next month, but we left autoscale at default.
[01:20] Diego: Quick note: we observed tail latency correlated with long context windows plus a higher-than-normal tokenization rate for some customer prompts. There was also a model swap (v1.3 -> v1.5) in the catalog that increased per-token cost a little.
[01:37] Ethan: Ok. From infra side, we can send you the traffic patterns, but want to understand the tradeoffs: if we lock in Dedicated for peak, what's the fallback when demand exceeds pool?
[01:47] Maya: Good question. Redwood policy today is to route by priority — canary to Dedicated with burst fallback to hosted variants. We can configure autoscale thresholds and a warm standby pool. For Halcyon we can set a soft limit so the fallback only happens after X minutes or percent utilization.
[02:03] Priya R. (Finance): From our angle we need predictable monthly spend — the December surprise damaged our forecast. Can you show a pricing example for Reserved capacity and how unit costs drop vs hosted pay-as-you-go?
[02:15] Maya: Absolutely. We'll send a pilot pricing matrix showing Reserved monthly commits, expected token cost per 1M tokens, and breakeven horizon. We'll include sensitivity to burst traffic.
[02:26] Sofia: Also, security question — our legal wants a SOC2 summary and details about KMS keying for EU data. We had to pause a rollout in France until we confirm residency and audit logs.
[02:38] Diego: We have a SOC2 summary pack, and Private deployment options with customer-managed KMS for on-prem or VPC. We'll attach the SOC2 doc and the KMS integration notes after the call.
[02:49] Ethan: For the benchmark, we want end-to-end realism — 95th percentile latency, token throughput, KV cache hit rates, and cost per 1M tokens measured on our sample workload. Also can you include quantization/profile recommendations?
[03:03] Priya (SE): Yes — we'll propose a 2-hour benchmark run. Steps: 1) customer provides traffic pattern and sample prompts 2) Redwood configures a Dedicated pool with suggested batching settings and optional prefix cache 3) run controlled load against both Hosted and Dedicated variants 4) measure latency, CPU/GPU utilization, token cost, and quality drift metrics.
[03:24] Sofia: How long does it typically take to provision Dedicated for a test? We need it by the week of 1/26.
[03:30] Maya: For trials we can provision a small pool in 48-72 hours once the commitment is in place. We'll aim for that week.
[03:36] Diego: One operational caveat: if you use long context models with large kv caches, the memory pressure can reduce throughput; our Optimize team recommends a mixed model approach — smaller context for interactive, bigger for batch.
[03:49] Ethan: Noted. On the financial side — can you model worst-case cost if we keep hosted and have two more spikes like December in Q1? Priya R. is worried about burn.
[03:59] Priya R.: Yes. We need a delta model: baseline hosted cost, hosted with two additional spikes, and a reserved commit with burst overlay.
[04:08] Maya: We'll include that in the pilot pricing document. We'll also surface the expected cost savings from caching and quantization where applicable — usually 15-40% depending on workload.
[04:18] Sofia: About observability — the console dashboards helped but we need more granular per-route token-level breakdowns and alerting tied to prompt sets. Can Redwood attach SLO alerts to token burn thresholds?
[04:29] Priya (SE): Yes, we can configure token burn alerts and per-route dashboards. Also suggest adding tracing hooks from your app to Redwood so we can correlate user requests to model latency.
[04:41] Ethan: One more ask: for EU regulation we need audit logs with field-level redaction possibilities and retention controls. Is that available in Private?
[04:50] Diego: Private has longer retention and KMS options; hosted supports exportable audit logs and configurable retention on enterprise tiers. We'll provide a short matrix of retention features by deployment mode.
[04:59] Sofia: Great. Moving to roadmap alignment — our product roadmap has model rollouts in March and June. We want to avoid surprises during rollout. Can Redwood support canary routing and automatic rollback on quality regressions?
[05:12] Priya (SE): Yes — Redwood has rollout policies: canary, A/B, and automatic fallback based on defined regressions (prompt set evals). We recommend running small canaries in staging with the same traffic profile.
[05:23] Maya: We can also run pre-rollout evals against your golden prompt sets. Diego, remind them about automatic regression alerts and the eval dashboard.
[05:31] Diego: Right — we'll set up an eval suite. We can tie regression alerts to Slack or ops pager if you want.
[05:37] Ethan: That would be helpful.
[05:40] Sofia: Ok recap please — who owns what and dates?
[05:43] Maya: Sure — next steps: Maya will send the pilot pricing and ROI sheet by 1/22; Priya Patel will send benchmark plan and metrics checklist by 1/23; Ethan to share traffic patterns and preferred regions by 1/21. SOC2 and KMS docs will be attached by Diego after the call. We'll target the week of 1/26 for a 2-hour benchmark.
[05:59] Priya R.: Sounds good. Quick question — any known risk if we enable prefix caching across mixed models?
[06:05] Priya (SE): Risk is minimal but watch for cache pollution if prompts vary widely; we'll recommend prompt normalization and a TTL business rule.
[06:13] Sofia: Thank you everyone. Anything else?
[06:16] Maya: One last note — you mentioned Anthropic and CloudX earlier. If you evaluate competitors, we can provide side-by-side latency and cost reads from our public benchmarks but we recommend running your own benchmark.
[06:29] Ethan: Agreed. Thanks.
[06:31] Meeting end / small chitchat 6:31-6:45

Notes and Links referenced: 1) Pilot pricing template (link sent after call) 2) SOC2 summary (attach) 3) Benchmark plan doc (to be shared) 4) Eval prompt set spreadsheet (customer to provide)
